Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Astrawell pilot — ask for one-time onboarding credit

Kimberly,

Quick context: Astrawell (health-tech prospect) signed an MSA in principle and wants to run a 3-month private pilot on Dedicated capacity (VPC). They shared conservative usage forecasts (attached) but expect a sharp ramp if early evals look good. Procurement pushed back on standard onboarding fees and asked for a one-time onboarding credit to offset initial runtime costs while they validate.

What I'm asking: Can we get VP/CFO leadership to authorize a one-time onboarding credit of 30% (applied to first 3 months of usage charges) for DL-2026-578-AW? Rationale below and mitigations:
- Upside: Astrawell is a regulated provider in our vertical; pilot could convert to a $600k ARR committed deployment within 12 months if model performance passes clinical checks.
- Risk: Short-term margin pressure on Dedicated GPU pools; initial months could be below break-even without credit.
- Mitigations I propose: 1) billing floor of $15k/month during pilot (offsets fixed infra) 2) 12-month conversion clause with minimum committed spend if they convert 3) escalate to finance for usage monitoring and weekly cadence during pilot.

Attachments: term_sheet_v3.pdf (commercial term sheet), usage_forecast.xlsx (monthly token & seat plan). HubSpot link included below.

If you want a shorter memo for Marcus / CFO, I can draft a two-paragraph exec memo with contribution analysis — attaching a suggested template.

Thanks,
Priyom
---

Kim / Priyom,

I reviewed the term sheet and ran a quick sensitivity using the attached executive memo (exec_memo_astrawell.docx). Bottom line: I can support a concession but recommend a lower one-time credit to protect gross margins. My suggested options for Marcus/CFO:

Option A (preferred): 20% onboarding credit applied to first 2 months + $15k/month floor during pilot + explicit conversion commitment (12 months, min $150k ARR).
Option B (riskier): 30% onboarding credit (first 3 months) only if Astrawell signs LOI for 12-month conversion within 30 days of pilot completion and provides a refundable deposit equal to one month’s floor.

I also recommend adding a billing holdback clause (we bill, but 25% of credit is deferred until conversion) to reduce churn risk. Legal flagged two minor redlines on the conversion term (we'll tighten timelines).

I'm happy to present either option to Marcus; I slightly favor Option A to keep runway shorter and align incentives.

Marissa
